summary: The Clarendon Fund is the University of Oxford's graduate scholarship scheme for new Master's and DPhil students. It aims to let the most academically able students study at Oxford, whatever their country or subject. There is no separate scholarship application: every applicant who applies to an eligible course by the course's December or January deadline is considered. Awards pay the course fee and a grant towards living costs.
eligibility_notes:
Open to applicants for graduate study at Oxford. There are no limits on nationality, country of ordinary residence or field of study. All full-time and part-time DPhil and Master's courses are covered. Applicants with Home, Republic of Ireland, Islands or Overseas fee status can all be considered.

You are considered automatically if you apply to your course by the December or January deadline that applies to that course. Scholars are chosen for outstanding academic merit and potential, and the competition is described as highly competitive.

Not eligible: holders of a deferred graduate offer, and current Oxford students who will simply continue the same degree. A current Master's student who applies for a DPhil or a second Master's can be considered. As a guideline, most scholars hold at least a first class degree or equivalent (for example GPA 3.7 out of 4); a strong Master's can offset a weaker first degree.
funding_summary: A Clarendon award pays the course fee and a grant towards living costs. For full-time scholars the living grant is set by reference to the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend. Both are paid for the period in which the scholar is liable for fees, which can be up to four years on a DPhil. Part-time scholars receive a study support grant that is a share of the full-time rate rather than the full amount.
programmes_note: All full-time and part-time DPhil and Master's courses are eligible; the scheme is not limited by subject. The scheme is for new courses.
institutions_note: Tenable at the University of Oxford only. Oxford colleges and faculties also add their own awards that are linked to Clarendon, for example Wolfson College (several named scholarships for 2027-28), Christ Church (eight awards, normally one in each of four divisions) and University College (one award in the Humanities and one in the Social Sciences for October 2027 entry). These need no separate application: they use the same graduate application and deadline.

requirements.text: No separate scholarship application and no separate scholarship documents. The Oxford graduate course application is used, with the documents that your course asks for (for example transcripts, references, personal statement, research proposal where required).

Applicants must meet the course's December or January deadline. The list of documents belongs to each course and was not readable on the central Oxford pages (blocked); check the course page for the exact list.

application_steps.title: Apply to an eligible Oxford course by its deadline
application_steps.detail: Submit the normal Oxford graduate application for a new full-time or part-time Master's or DPhil by the December or January deadline of your course. No separate Clarendon application exists; applicants who meet the deadline are considered automatically. Faculty pages for Law and Theology name the January deadline; Social Policy and Intervention gives a department date in January 2027.

application_steps.title: Check college-linked and named Clarendon awards
application_steps.detail: Colleges such as Wolfson, Christ Church and University College add awards linked to Clarendon. They also need no separate application: the same graduate application and deadline are used, and those colleges describe their awards on their own pages.

application_steps.title: Faculty assesses and nominates candidates
application_steps.detail: Your admitting faculty or department assesses your application as part of normal admissions and decides whom to nominate for a Clarendon scholarship. In the Humanities Division a divisional selection panel then chooses among the nominated candidates; the English Faculty states about 35 awards a year in that division. Selection is on academic merit and potential.

application_steps.title: Wait for the result; no news by mid-June means no award
application_steps.detail: Stored data (carried over from the central Oxford pages): most first Clarendon offers are sent by the end of April, and an applicant not contacted by mid-June should assume the application was unsuccessful. The faculty pages read do not give result dates.

application_steps.title: Award runs for the period of fee liability
application_steps.detail: A scholar receives the course fee and a living grant for the fee liability period (up to four years on a DPhil depending on the course). Terms of acceptance, payment dates and obligations are set in the offer letter and are not described on the pages read.
